title: Certified Edge Unlearning for Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Edge unlearning in GNNs requires training a model as if specified edges never existed in the original graph.

gap.claim: Graph edge dependencies can make conventional unlearning incomplete, while retraining from scratch is computationally expensive.

contributions.claim: CEU is a certified edge-unlearning framework for GNNs.
CEU updates a pretrained GNN in a single step to remove the influence of specified edges.
CEU has a theoretical guarantee under a convexity assumption on the loss function.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that CEU achieves speedup gains over retraining and existing unlearning methods for linear and deep GNNs.
The authors report that CEU maintains model accuracy comparable to retraining from scratch.

narrative_sequence.summary: Privacy policies and regulations motivate interest in machine unlearning.
The paper focuses on edge unlearning in GNNs, where correlated edges complicate complete removal of influence.
Retraining without the specified edges can remove their influence but has high computational cost.
CEU performs a single-step parameter update on a pretrained GNN and provides a convexity-based theoretical guarantee.
The authors report speedups and comparable accuracy for linear and deep GNNs.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, evaluation metrics, or exact speedup values.
The abstract does not state the scope or practical implications of the convexity assumption.
